content:
maria: noticed a 20-30% uptick in first-token latency on /v1/chat-stream starting ~3312343000, seems correlated with the kernel-selector tweak rolled last night. TTFT from p95 went 220ms -> 280ms. can we quickly pinpoint if this is queueing vs kernel handoff?

kai: saw that too. sample traces show an extra ~45ms in a field called kernel_handoff_ms for many traces. unclear if it's our scheduler or a kernel slowdown. attaching probe summary below.

perf-bot: automated-probe: route=/v1/chat-stream samples=1200 window=15m p50_ttft=125ms p95_ttft=282ms p99_ttft=520ms avg_kernel_handoff_ms=46.3 avg_queue_ms=11.8 avg_decode_ms=88.6 kv_cache_hit_rate=0.83

kai: pasted a small probe query i ran:
```
SELECT route, percentile(ttft, 95) as p95, avg(kernel_handoff_ms) FROM token_traces
WHERE route='/v1/chat-stream' AND ts > now()-15m GROUP BY route;
```
results: p95 282ms kernel_handoff avg 46ms

tyler: quick thought: the kernel selector change added a new condition to prefer microkernel v2 for short contexts which increased kernel init path for some sequences. microkernel v2 has a slightly higher handshake latency but lower steady-state throughput. if our traces are sampling at token 0 vs token 5 we might be seeing amortization issues.

devon: +1 on amortization. we need token-level breakdown that separates: prequeue_wait, queue_ms, kernel_init_ms, kernel_handoff_ms, kernel_exec_ms, kv_lookup_ms, decode_ms. current dashboards show only queue|decode|other which hides the handoff.

maria: agree. proposal: add these fields at sampling rate 1% to limit cardinality and tag by model_variant, kernel_id, softbatch_size, route. dashboards: per-route TTFT waterfall with stacked bars (prequeue, queue, handoff, kernel, decode, kv).

kai: implementation note: we already have kernel_selector logs that print kernel_id and decision_reason. can emit kernel_init_start/count markers to correlate with traces. also add a short-lived probe that forces microkernel v1 for 1% of traffic on the route to A/B.

tyler: for A/B we can add a routing policy:
```json
{"route": "/v1/chat-stream", "policy": {"force_kernel": "microkernel_v1", "sample_rate": 0.01}}
```
this will let us isolate kernel-level amortization without changing wider traffic.

devon: dashboard ask: add a small table card that shows recent regressions by route: delta p95_ttft (30m vs 6h), delta kernel_handoff_ms, delta kv_hit_rate. also add an annotation when we flip kernel selector commits.

maria: also observed kv cache hit_rate dipped from 0.89 -> 0.83 for the same window. could be related if prefetch overlap was disabled in the selector change. kai can you confirm if prefetch toggles were touched?

kai: i rolled back the prefetch flag to its prior default in canary at 3312344000 for two hosts, but the global change was later. logs show prefetch_overlap=false for microkernel_v2 in the new selector. that would explain extra kernel lookups and vm syncs.

maria: ok action items: 1) kai to run 1% microkernel_v1 A/B and collect token-level traces (owner: kai, due: 3312345900). 2) devon to add token-breakdown fields to tracing schema and a dashboard prototype (owner: devon, due: 3312346500). 3) tyler to add annotation hook to deployments and kernel-selector commits (owner: tyler, due: 3312346200). 4) I will open a rollback PR for the selector change if A/B shows kernel_handoff regression (owner: maria, pending A/B).

devon: for instrumentation new fields we should keep names stable: prequeue_wait_ms, queue_ms, kernel_init_ms, kernel_handoff_ms, kernel_exec_ms, kv_lookup_ms, kv_prefetch_ms, decode_ms. sample at 1% but ensure we always include sample_id and model_variant to join logs.

kai: quick example trace (synthetic, single token):
```
trace_id=abc123 route=/v1/chat-stream sample_id=42 model=redwood-ggml microkernel= v2
prequeue_wait_ms=2 queue_ms=9 kernel_init_ms=18 kernel_handoff_ms=47 kernel_exec_ms=60 kv_lookup_ms=3 decode_ms=75
```
shows kernel_handoff dominating a single-token TTFT spike.

maria: that aligns with production p95. if A/B proves microkernel_v2 is the culprit we should revert selector changes and add a follow-up to optimize handshake in microkernel_v2. also consider warming kernels proactively for routes with short sequences.

tyler: note on warming: we can add quick warmup on route hotstart with an async 1-token warm call to create KV leases and kernel contexts but must be careful about cost. propose a configurable warm_count threshold (e.g., warm if rate>50r/s).

perf-bot: scheduled-run: running canary A/B now (sample_rate=1%). expect telemetry in ~10m.

maria: thanks all. please drop short updates in this thread when you have numbers. i'll keep an eye on alerts and will PR rollback if A/B shows clear regression. :+1:
